title: Plumbers Salary: Award Rates vs National Minimum Wage in 2026
description: Compare plumbers salary under the Plumbing and Fire Sprinklers Award with the National Minimum Wage. See hourly rates, casual loading, super, and tax estimates.
salarySummary: A qualified plumber under the Plumbing and Fire Sprinklers Award earns at least $29.45 per hour as a tradesperson Level 1, well above the National Minimum Wage of $26.44 per hour for a 38-hour week.

faqs.q: What is the minimum hourly rate for a plumber under the award?
faqs.a: Under the Plumbing and Fire Sprinklers Award 2020, a Plumbing and mechanical services tradesperson Level 1 earns a minimum weekly rate of $1,119.10 for 38 hours, which is $29.45 per hour. Higher classifications, such as Advanced tradesperson Level 2, pay up to $33.77 per hour. These rates are from the award text and apply from 1 July 2025 (the most recent update). Casual employees receive an additional 25% loading on top of these hourly rates.

faqs.q: How does casual loading affect a plumber's pay?
faqs.a: Casual employees under the award are paid an extra 25% on top of the minimum hourly rate. For a tradesperson Level 1, that means $29.45 × 1.25 = $36.81 per hour. The loading compensates for not receiving paid leave or other entitlements. The [casual loading](/topics/casual-loading) page explains how to calculate it using our timesheet tool.

faqs.q: Is superannuation included in the hourly rate or paid on top?
faqs.a: Superannuation is paid on top of the hourly rate. Under the award and the Superannuation Guarantee, employers must contribute 12% of ordinary earnings (from 1 July 2026) into a super fund. For a full-time plumber earning $29.45 per hour, that adds about $3.53 per hour in super, but it is not part of the hourly wage. The [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging) page has more details.

bodyMarkdown:
## Plumbers Salary Under the Plumbing and Fire Sprinklers Award

If you are looking up a **plumbers salary**, the first thing to know is that most plumbers in Australia are covered by the **Plumbing and Fire Sprinklers Award 2020**. This award sets minimum pay rates that are higher than the National Minimum Wage. For example, a qualified tradesperson (Level 1) must be paid at least **$29.45 per hour** or **$1,119.10 per week** for a 38-hour week. Compare that to the National Minimum Wage of $26.44 per hour – a difference of over $3 per hour.

### How to Calculate Annual Pay from an Hourly Rate

The standard formula for annual gross pay is:

**Hourly rate × hours per week × 52**

For a full-time plumber working 38 hours per week at $29.45 per hour:

$29.45 × 38 × 52 = **$58,193.20 per year**

This assumes the same rate every week with no unpaid overtime, penalty rates, or allowances. If you are paid fortnightly, multiply the weekly rate by 2: $1,119.10 × 2 = **$2,238.20 per fortnight**.

### National Minimum Wage vs Award Rates

The National Minimum Wage from 1 July 2026 is $26.44 per hour ($1,004.90 per week for 38 hours). Casual employees get $33.05 per hour including the 25% loading. However, the Plumbing Award sets higher minimums for most classifications. For instance, a Plumbing and mechanical services worker Level 1(a) (new entrant) starts at $26.67 per hour, still above the national minimum. As you progress through levels, the rates increase. The award also includes allowances for tools, special work, and travel that can boost take-home pay.

### Casual Loading for Plumbers

Casual employees under the award receive a **25% loading** on top of the minimum hourly rate. For a tradesperson Level 1, that is $29.45 × 1.25 = **$36.81 per hour**. The loading is meant to compensate for not receiving paid annual leave, sick leave, or other entitlements. Our [timesheet](/) tool lets you enter a base hourly rate and check a box to add the 25% casual loading automatically – never enter a rate that already includes the loading.

### Superannuation Paid on Top

Employers must pay superannuation of **12% of ordinary earnings** (from 1 July 2026) into a complying super fund. This is on top of the hourly wage. For a full-time plumber earning $58,193.20 per year, the employer adds about **$6,983.18** in super, up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830. Super does not reduce your take-home pay; it is an extra benefit.

### Tax and Medicare Levy

Using the 2026–27 resident tax rates:

- Nil tax on the first $18,200
- 15% on income between $18,201 and $45,000
- 30% on income between $45,001 and $135,000
- 37% on income between $135,001 and $190,000
- 45% on income above $190,000

Plus the **Medicare levy** of 2% (using 2025–26 single reduction thresholds as 2026–27 thresholds are not yet confirmed). For a plumber earning $58,193.20, the estimated tax is about $8,897 plus Medicare of $1,164, leaving an after-tax income of approximately **$48,132**.

### Other Award Classifications

The award has many levels. For example, an Advanced plumbing and mechanical services tradesperson Level 2 earns **$33.77 per hour** ($1,283.10 per week). That annualises to $66,769.52. A Sprinkler fitter tradesperson has similar rates. The [reference tables](/data) on our site list all classifications.

### Using the Timesheet Tool

To estimate your own pay, use our [timesheet](/) tool. Enter your base hourly rate (e.g., $29.45 for a tradesperson), select 38 hours per week, and the tool will show annual gross, fortnightly pay, tax, Medicare, and super. If you are casual, tick the casual loading box – the tool adds 25% on top of the base rate.

### Summary

A **plumbers salary** under the award is significantly above the National Minimum Wage. The minimum for a qualified tradesperson is $29.45 per hour, with higher rates for advanced skills. Casual workers get a 25% loading. Super is paid on top at 12%. Use the formula hourly × 38 × 52 to get annual gross, then subtract tax and Medicare for an estimate of take-home pay. For precise calculations, always refer to the award and the [pay guides](/blog) from the Fair Work Ombudsman.
